newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open higher, all eyes on jobs report.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open higher, all eyes on jobs report.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries opened with a slightly better tone on Friday, with this morning's employment report expected to provide the market with direction the rest of the day.
Ahead of the April jobs data, the 30-year bond was at 96-13/32, up 2/32 from Thursday. Its yield edged down to 6.91 percent, its lowest level since closing at 6.88 percent on March 12.
The Labor Department will release the jobs report at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. Non-farm payrolls are seen up 211,000 in Aprll, after a 175,000 gain in March, according to a Reuters poll.

Traders said the market would be content if payrolls were up 200,000, with the unemployment rate at 5.2 percent in April. "That would show the economy is OK and the Fed won't have to tighten again," said a trader at a U.S. bank.
"The market is all bulled up," he added. "That market wants to go higher and if (economic) news allows it to blast off, it will."
He noted that the market is in "great" technical shape, aided by the buying of coupons in recent sessions by the Federal Reserve.

Treasuries had been somewhat lower heading into the U.S. session. Light buying early in the Tokyo session was said to have quickly evaporated, and selling -- mainly in the short and intermediate sectors -- continued into the London session.
Comments by New York Fed president William McDonough that inflation was well behaved gave mild support to Treasuries.

But an article in Business Week saying that Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan expects the economy to slow in the current quarter and growth in 1997 to moderate led to short-covering early in the New York session, bringing Treasuries off its lows.

Also on Friday, due at 1000 EDT, are the index of leading indicators for March and the University of Michigan's consumer-sentiment index. Both reports are expected to be largely ignored, as the jobs data are the main focus.
Meanwhile, the market is eyeing the budget talks. A budget pact could come as early as today, which is seen as adding to the market's positive tone.
The two-year note was up 1/32 at 100-8/32 to yield 6.24 percent. The 10-year note was up 2/32 at 97-1/32 to yield 6.67 percent.
